A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 34 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–R, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations, CIFAR-10 likelihood-estimation experiments, high-density image-generation results, and blur analyses, including additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the main-text experiments, Table 2 likelihood comparisons and Stable Diffusion examples in the appendices.

M1.justification: The augmented likelihood-tracking dynamics, mode-tracking procedure, HD-ODE approximation and Algorithm 1 retain the same equations and procedural steps.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same Gaussian simulations, CIFAR-10, ImageNet-64, FFHQ-256, Churches-256 and text-to-image examples in Appendix O. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain PF-ODE, reverse-SDE and the original pretrained-model samplers, including stochastic Heun and Predictor-Corrector sampling in Appendix N. The new related-work citations are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Training settings, likelihood metrics and sampling procedures are unchanged. Both retain the main-text 512-sample comparisons, Appendix N's 1024 CIFAR samples and 192 samples for other models per strategy, and the seven blur strengths.

E4.justification: The likelihood-estimation bias analysis, threshold sweeps, blur and compression-size analyses, discontinuous mode-tracking example in Appendix J, and image-detail comparisons in Appendix P are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Appendix N and Table 2 retain the same mean ± one standard deviation reporting. No seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 2 entries and plotted results are unchanged. For example, FFHQ256 retains NLL values of 1.01 ± 0.41 for Original and -4.01 ± 0.96 for HD(t = 0.3T); Section 3.2 retains correlations of 0.996 and 0.999.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorems 1–7, propositions, Corollary 1, Lemma 1 and appendix proofs are unchanged. Citation updates do not alter the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution summary and conclusion retain the same claims about economical SDE likelihood tracking, mode tracking, high-density sampling and cartoon-like or blurry high-density images.

C2.justification: The interpretations and applicability limitations are retained. Section 4.2 changes 'costly' to 'prohibitively expensive', but this limitation was already explicitly stated in v2's Appendix R and supported by Appendix K.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project code-repository link in the abstract, providing access information absent from v2. Implementation hyperparameters and experimental details in Appendices M–N remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds Park et al. (2024) on sampling temperature and cartoon-like outputs, and acknowledges Skreta et al. (2025) independently discovering Theorem 1 and Lemma 1 while distinguishing the forward-process and imperfect-score contributions. Other reference changes mainly update existing works' publication metadata.

P1.justification: v4 lightly rewrites Section 7, strengthens the wording about computational cost and standardizes bibliography entries and citation years. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The expanded abstract and text edits produce modest layout reflow, including shifted placement of Figures 4–5 and redistribution of references across pages. Figures, table structures, axes, legends and visual examples are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added code-access pointer improves discoverability, while Section 7 more clearly acknowledges related and concurrent contributions and identifies their overlap. These are useful but limited improvements; the method, theoretical development and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
